_meta.purpose: Propose-only sister-project charter for testing model handling of laws, protections, and remedy routing in developing-country and low-documentation regulatory contexts.
_meta.status: propose-only -- this charter is planning metadata, not source-verified legal content, not worker-facing advice, and not benchmark evidence.

research_question: Can models handle local laws, regulations, protections, complaint paths, and source uncertainty in lower-documentation jurisdictions without hallucinating authority, overgeneralizing from better documented regimes, or creating safety risk?
target_jurisdiction_families: East Africa origin and destination states
West Africa origin and destination states
Latin America origin and destination states
Gulf and other destination corridors only after concrete forum scope
port, flag, and crew-nationality jurisdictions for maritime work
benchmark_axes: local law versus international anchor discipline
date and version sensitivity for volatile rules
informal publication handling for social-channel notices and scanned circulars
ordinary protection detection beyond trafficking labels
safe remedy routing with privacy and retaliation caveats
source abstention when local-law coverage is missing
source_admission_rules: Every scored local-law claim needs a dated source object with authority, jurisdiction, publication date or access date, and archive status.
International instruments may anchor reasoning but cannot substitute for source-verified local law.
Social-channel notices, scanned circulars, and informal registries are source leads until archived, dated, and public-interest reviewed.
Public complaint lists, case rows, names, contacts, addresses, and small-community identifiers are rejected unless fully redacted into aggregate patterns.
Complaint paths and remedy channels must name the concrete forum or regulator scope, not a broad corridor label.
Expert or practitioner review is required before public claims, training use, or comparable benchmark scoring.
scored_capabilities: identifies the rights trigger and the vulnerable party
selects the relevant origin, destination, forum, flag, port, or regulator jurisdiction
separates verified local law from international anchors and unresolved source gaps
detects ordinary labour, wage, housing, credit, education, injury, and consumer protections
routes to plausible remedy channels without exposing private details or retaliation risk
refuses to invent fee caps, license status, hotline numbers, dates, office names, or legal certainty

readiness_gates.description: Each prompt jurisdiction and protection category has dated source-object coverage.
Broad corridor, forum, flag, port, and regulator labels are resolved into concrete jurisdictions.
Source candidates exclude names, contacts, addresses, private cases, and small-community identifiers.
A practitioner or domain expert reviews local-law mappings and remedy paths.
The runner has source-verified RAG or tool grounding for the domain.

first_build_phases.description: Validate and render the sister-project charter as a planning artifact.
Use the existing domain curation bundle to expose source gaps for the worker-protections seed.
Use the regulatory curation bundle to stage adjacent candidate domains without creating prompts.
Run only isolated diagnostics after source gaps are explicit and unresolved source gaps are scored as abstention discipline.

non_goals: It is not a legal advice product.
It is not a worker-facing referral system.
It is not a claim that country-law coverage is complete.
It is not a prompt-generation shortcut for unverified local rules.
It is not comparable leaderboard evidence until every readiness gate passes.
